sections.h2: What a quitclaim deed passes on
sections.html:
A quitclaim deed gives the buyer or relative whatever the signer owns in the parcel, and promises nothing about how solid that ownership is. The McCracken County Clerk describes it as a deed that works by release: it passes any title or claim the grantor may have, with no warranty or covenants for title.

Kentucky gives warranty deeds their own wording. Under KRS 382.030, the words 'with general warranty' become a promise to defend the property against all persons, and KRS 382.040 narrows that promise to claims made by or through the grantor. A quitclaim carries neither promise.

That is why quitclaims turn up between relatives, former spouses and co-heirs, and in cleanups of an old record. A buyer paying full price usually wants more than a quitclaim in the chain. If you plan to resell afterward, mention the quitclaim to the closing agent early so the title search can allow for it.

  • It conveys the grantor's interest, large or small, as it stands on the day of signing.
  • It does not create ownership the grantor never had.
  • It does not remove a mortgage, a judgment lien or an unpaid tax lien from the parcel.

sections.h2: What the deed must contain to be recorded
sections.html:
KRS 382.135(1) sets out what every deed to real property needs, and a quitclaim counts as a deed for this purpose. The clerk cannot accept a deed that falls short, so a missing line means a rejected filing and a second trip to the courthouse.

  • Full name and mailing address of both the grantor and the grantee.
  • A statement of the full consideration.
  • An in-care-of address where the tax bill for the transfer year can be sent.
  • A sworn, notarized certificate signed by both sides. It either confirms the consideration or states that the transfer is a gift and gives the estimated fair cash value.

Two more statutes add to the list. KRS 382.335 calls for a signed statement naming whoever prepared the deed, with that person's address, plus the grantee's mailing address. KRS 382.110 wants the deed to point back to the grantor's source of title: book and page if the title came by recorded deed, or a plain account of how and from whom it arrived if it came by inheritance. Under KRS 382.130, a deed made in Kentucky can go to record on the maker's acknowledgment before the clerk or a notary.

sections.h2: Where to record it and what it costs
sections.html:
File with the county clerk where the land lies. If a parcel straddles a county line, use the county that holds the larger share. KRS 382.110(1) sets that rule. Fees come from KRS 64.012 and the transfer tax from KRS 142.050.

Kentucky charges for recording a deed
ChargeAmount
Recording and indexing, up to 5 pages$33, of which $27 stays with the clerk and $6 goes to the affordable housing trust fund
Each page after the fifth$3
Each added reference to the same instrument$4
Permanent records storage reimbursement$10 under KRS 64.012(3)(a)
Real estate transfer tax, paid by the grantor$0.50 for each $500 of value or fraction of $500

Counties post their own totals. McCracken County's clerk publishes a $50 deed filing fee with the same $3 charge for pages past five. Phone the clerk where your parcel sits and get the all-in number before you drive over.

KRS 142.050 puts the tax on the grantor, and the clerk collects it before taking the deed. On a sale it is figured on the full consideration, liens included. On a gift, or when the deed shows a token price, the statute substitutes the estimated open-market value. The clerk does the math, which is why a deed that understates the price draws questions.

Subsection (7) lists the exempt transfers. These are the ones a quitclaim most often involves:

  • Parent to child, or grandparent to grandchild, for a token price only.
  • One spouse to the other, or between former spouses in a divorce.
  • A deed that only confirms or corrects an earlier recorded deed.
  • A transfer made solely to secure or release a debt.
  • Partition, foreclosure, or a voluntary surrender in lieu of foreclosure.
  • A trustee to a successor trustee, and certain moves into a trust whose only beneficiary is the grantor.

An exemption waives the tax, not the paperwork. A gift deed from mother to daughter still needs the notarized fair cash value certificate under KRS 382.135 even though no tax is owed.

sections.h2: If the grantor inherited the property
sections.html:
A deed from someone who took title by descent needs one extra document. Under KRS 382.120, the grantor, any heir at law, or two Kentucky residents with personal knowledge must give the clerk an affidavit before the deed is filed. It names the person who died, the date of death, whether that person was married, where they lived and that they died without a will, and it lists each heir with age, address, relationship and share.

The clerk records the affidavit, indexes it under the ancestor as grantor and each heir as grantee, and charges the same fees as for a deed. KRS 382.135(4) adds a duty for estates passing by will or intestacy: before the estate closes, the personal representative files an affidavit in each county where land lies, naming who receives each parcel and its estimated value. Heirs quitclaiming to one another to consolidate a family house should make sure both affidavits are on file first, since the clerk will not take the deed ahead of them.

sections.h2: Penalties for a false statement on a deed
sections.html:
KRS 382.990 attaches criminal penalties to deed paperwork. Willfully and fraudulently giving a false statement of the full actual consideration, or of the full estimated value, under KRS 382.135 is a Class D felony. Knowingly swearing to a false statement in the descent affidavit under KRS 382.120 is a Class A misdemeanor, and the person is liable to anyone injured by its use.

Write the true figure. If a family member is paying a token amount for a house worth far more, say so on the deed and let the clerk compute tax on market value or apply the parent and child exemption. Shaving a few dollars off transfer tax by understating the price leaves a recorded document that can be challenged later, and a future buyer's title company will read it.

sections.h2: Does a quitclaim help when you plan to sell?
sections.html:
Sometimes. It can put the title into the right names so a sale can close, and it can also cause delay. A quitclaim leaves every lien and tax debt in place. KRS 382.070 adds a warning: a seller who leaves part of the price unpaid has no lien against creditors and purchasers unless the deed states what remains unpaid.

Owners who inherited a Kentucky house, fell behind on payments or hold a property with repair problems often ask whether a quitclaim to a relative will simplify things. The better first step is usually a payoff request to the lender and to the county for any unpaid tax, then a plain talk with a closing attorney. If you want a direct cash sale of a Kentucky house as it stands, a quitclaim signed beforehand does not change what the buyer's title company has to clear.

faqs.q: Do I need a lawyer to record a Kentucky quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: No statute requires one, but KRS 382.335 makes the deed show the name and address of the person who prepared it. Many people use an attorney or title company so the consideration certificate, source of title and legal description are right on the first filing.

faqs.q: Is a notary required on a quitclaim deed in Kentucky?
faqs.a: Yes. The grantor's signature must be acknowledged, and KRS 382.135 requires the consideration or gift certificate to be sworn and notarized by both sides. County clerk offices can notarize for a fee set in KRS 64.012, so ask the clerk before you sign anywhere else.

faqs.q: What does recording a Kentucky quitclaim deed cost?
faqs.a: State law sets $33 for up to five pages and $3 per extra page, and KRS 64.012 also allows a $10 records reimbursement. Transfer tax is fifty cents per $500 of value unless an exemption fits. McCracken County's clerk posts a $50 deed fee, so confirm the figure with the clerk who will record yours.

faqs.q: Can I quitclaim my house to my child and avoid transfer tax?
faqs.a: A transfer between parent and child for only a token price is exempt under KRS 142.050(7)(l). The deed still needs the sworn certificate that calls it a gift and states the estimated fair cash value.

faqs.q: Which office records a Kentucky quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: The county clerk where the property, or most of it, sits. A deed recorded in the wrong county fails to put later purchasers and creditors on notice, which is the protection the grantee needs.
